content.overview: Wildlife protection in India is governed primarily by the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, which provides for the protection of wild animals, birds and plants and for matters connected therewith, including protected areas such as sanctuaries and national parks and regulation of hunting and trade. Constitutional support appears in Article 48A and Article 51A(g). The framework sits alongside forest conservation law, the EPA and NGT jurisdiction.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Protected species or area? (2) Hunting/trade restriction? (3) Sanctuary or national park regime? (4) Constitutional duties?
content.study:
Distinguish wildlife protection (species and protected areas) from forest-land conversion control under the Forest (Conservation) Act. Always verify schedules and offence provisions against the current official text.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972
sections.body: Protects wild animals, birds and plants; regulates hunting; provides for sanctuaries, national parks and related protected areas; controls trade as enacted.

sections.heading: Protected areas
sections.body: Sanctuaries and national parks — activities restricted according to the statutory regime for each category.

sections.heading: Hunting and trade
sections.body: Hunting of scheduled wild animals and specified trade/possession are regulated or prohibited as the Act provides.

sections.heading: Constitutional support
sections.body: Art. 48A (safeguard wild life); Art. 51A(g) (protect natural environment and have compassion for living creatures).

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: Forest conservation, EPA and EIA may apply where projects affect wildlife habitats and forest land.

examples.title: Activity in a sanctuary
examples.body: A commercial activity is proposed inside a wildlife sanctuary without the permissions the Act requires — wildlife protection restrictions apply.

hypotheticals.question: Is forest diversion approval under the Forest (Conservation) Act enough when a national park is affected?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not by itself. Wildlife protected-area rules under the Wild Life (Protection) Act remain a separate statutory regime.

distinctions.title: Wildlife protection vs forest conservation
distinctions.left: Species, hunting, trade and protected areas under WPA 1972.
distinctions.right: Forest land dereservation/non-forest use under FCA 1980.

misconceptions.trap: Wildlife law only applies inside national parks.
misconceptions.correction: The Act also regulates scheduled species, hunting and trade more broadly; protected areas are one part of the scheme.
